title: The Economics of Prevention: A 2025 Perspective
summary: An analysis of why preventive care models are failing to gain traction despite clear economic benefits.

children.text: Preventive care is often cited as the holy grail of healthcare economics. The logic is simple: catch disease early, treat it cheaply, and avoid the catastrophic costs of chronic management. However, the current reimbursement landscape tells a different story.
While payers champion wellness, their fee schedules often prioritize procedural intervention. A 15-minute wellness check reimburses at a fraction of a diagnostic imaging scan.
Key Insight: We cannot expect a system designed for sick care to spontaneously generate wellness without a fundamental realignment of financial incentives.
